### Maxwell's Equations in Differential Form

| Law | Name | Differential Form | Physical Significance |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 1 | Gauss's Law for Electricity | $\nabla \cdot \mathbf{E} = \frac{\rho}{\varepsilon_0}$ | Electric charges are sources/sinks of $\mathbf{E}$. |
| 2 | Gauss's Law for Magnetism | $\nabla \cdot \mathbf{B} = 0$ | Monopoles do not exist; magnetic field lines are continuous loops. |
| 3 | Faraday's Law of Induction | $\nabla \times \mathbf{E} = -\frac{\partial \mathbf{B}}{\partial t}$ | Time-varying magnetic fields produce electric fields. |
| 4 | Ampere-Maxwell Law | $\nabla \times \mathbf{B} = \mu_0\mathbf{J} + \mu_0\varepsilon_0\frac{\partial \mathbf{E}}{\partial t}$ | Electric currents and time-varying electric fields produce magnetic fields. |
proTip: Memorize both differential and integral forms, along with the names of all four constituent laws.
